newsitem.title: JORDAN: Healthy demand on banks props up Amman bourse.
newsitem.headline: Healthy demand on banks props up Amman bourse.

text.p: Buoyant local and foreign demand on Tuesday which focused mainly on blue-chip bank stock bolstered the performance of the Amman bourse for the second day running, dealers said.

Arab Bank rose by two dinars to 257 dinars in busy trade amid heightened market expectations of an announcement soon by the bank's board to convene an extraordinary AGM to issue shareholders a long delayed bonus share, brokers said.
Seven of the 10 banking shares traded on Tuesday rose, pushing the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index up 0.84 percent to 161.32 points in healthy turnover of 1.8 million dinars.
Brokers said local demand helped push up Bank of Jordan by 0.17 dinars to 3.54 dinars in the highest daily price jump in trade worth a healthy 65,779 dinars.
The second busiest traded stock, Jordan National Bank, rose 0.04 dinars to 2.13 dinars in mainly foreign inspired demand.

Brokers say the bourse is generally stable amid growing foreign interest which resurfaced since Saturday and could signal the start of a repeat pattern of select bargain buying on cement and mining firms which the bourse witnessed last month.
Jordan Cement, which has been targeted by foreign investors, rose 0.04 dinars to 4.12 dinars in the busiest trade of the day, worth 523,369 dinars.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.61 percent to 81.92 points, 1.76 percent down from the start of the year.
